Parser enters htmlCurrentChar to decode the next character from the input buffer.
Reads the current byte from the input stream; a byte >= 0x80 triggers the encoding detection path.
htmlFindEncoding scans the input for a meta charset declaration and returns a newly allocated xmlChar* buffer containing the encoding name, or NULL if none is found.
The encoding name from the meta charset attribute is duplicated into a heap buffer; this buffer is later freed and then used-after-free.
If no encoding guess is found, the parser falls back to UTF-8; otherwise guess points to the heap-allocated encoding name.
The current charset is converted to a name string for comparison with the guessed encoding name.
If the guessed encoding matches the current charset, guess is freed and the path exits normally; otherwise execution continues to the vulnerable branch.
The heap buffer holding the encoding name is freed here, but guess is still used later in the error reporting path.
USE-AFTER-FREE: the freed guess pointer is passed to xmlFindCharEncodingHandler, which dereferences the dangling pointer to look up the encoding handler.
The freed pointer is dereferenced; if the freed memory has been reused or unmapped, this read itself can crash or return garbage.
Second USE-AFTER-FREE: the freed guess pointer is passed as the format argument to htmlParseErr, which reads the freed buffer when formatting the error message.
